'''Anatolii Asirovich Goldberg''' ({{langx|ru|Анатолий Асирович Гольдберг}}, {{langx|uk|Анатолій Асірович Гольдберг}}, {{langx|he|אנטולי גולדברג}}; April 2, 1930, in [[Kyiv]] &ndash; October 11, 2008, in [[Netanya]]) was a [[Soviet]] and [[Israel]]i [[mathematician]] working in [[complex analysis]]. His main area of research was the theory of [[entire function|entire]] and [[meromorphic]] functions.<ref>{{cite journal|mr=2502930|last1=Zarīchniĭ|first1=M. M.|last2=Skaskīv|first2=O. B.|last3=Sheremeta|first3=M. M.|title=Anatolīĭ Asīrovich Golʹdberg (April 2, 1930&ndash;October 11, 2008)|journal=Mat. Stud.|volume=30|year=2008|issue=2|page=214|language=Ukrainian|url=http://www.vntl.com/im/pdf/30_2_214_214.pdf|access-date=January 5, 2012|archive-date=December 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161226055931/http://www.vntl.com/im/pdf/30_2_214_214.pdf}}</ref>

==Life and work==

Goldberg received his PhD in 1955 from [[Lviv University]] under the direction
of Lev Volkovyski. He worked as a docent in [[Uzhhorod National University]] (1955&ndash;1963), then in [[University of Lviv|Lviv University]] (1963&ndash;1997), where he became a full professor in 1965, and in [[Bar Ilan University]] (1997&ndash;2008). Goldberg, jointly with [[Iossif Ostrovskii]] and [[Boris Levin]], was awarded the State Prize of Ukraine in 1992.

Among his main achievements are:
* construction of meromorphic functions with infinitely many deficient values,
* solution of the inverse problem of [[Nevanlinna theory]] for finitely many deficient values,
* development of the integral with respect to a semi-additive measure.

He authored a book {{harvtxt|Goldberg|Ostrovskii|2008}} and over 150 research papers.

Several things are named after him: Goldberg's examples,<ref name="Hayman">{{cite book|mr=0164038|first=W. K.|last=Hayman|author-link=Walter Hayman|title=Meromorphic functions|url=https://archive.org/details/meromorphicfunct0000haym|url-access=registration|location=Oxford|publisher=Clarendon Press|year=1964}}</ref>
Goldberg's constants,<ref name="be">W. Bergweiler and [[Alexandre Eremenko|A. Eremenko]], 
[https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.2296 Goldberg's constants]</ref> and Goldberg's conjecture.<ref name="langley">{{cite journal|last=Langley|first=J.K.|mr=1447956|title=On the zeros of the second derivative|journal=Proc. R. Soc. Edinburgh Sect. A|volume=127|year=1997|issue=2|pages=359&ndash;368|doi=10.1017/S0308210500023672|s2cid=122636024 }}</ref>
<ref name="yamanoi">{{cite journal|last=Yamanoi|first=K.|mr=3056292|title=Zeros of higher derivatives of meromorphic functions in the complex plane|journal=Proc. London Math. Soc.|volume=106|year=2013|issue=4|pages=703&ndash;780|doi=10.1112/plms/pds051 |s2cid=122533496 }}</ref>
